D12·cm2z — 2026-09-16
rule: No perf claim below ±20% without an interleaved A/B (n ≥ 25, same record and session) and the load average noted; the Phase 3.3 gate re-records the reference in the same sitting as the candidate.
chose: Standing perf method while round 1 (or any benchmark) occupies this machine: every latency claim is an INTERLEAVED A/B (ABAB, order alternating per iteration), n ≥ 25, same record and same session id for both sides, with the 1-minute load average recorded in the perf JSON. Single-order A-then-B runs are indicative only. The 1.3 runner gains SOFAR_PERF_AB_BIN (a comparator spawned interleaved with every measured spawn, stats in `ab`) and a `load` header; the read paths on the real record use r1-fixes' shared harness `npm run bench:read-paths` (r1-fixes D18) so both records report the same table.
over: Trusting the single-order 1.3 numbers at the 10 ms scale; a rust-core-only interleaving harness that r1-fixes cannot run.
because: r1-fixes could not reproduce rust-core's +11/+12 ms read-path drift when measuring interleaved (session-start +0.5, user-prompt +3.4); round 1 runs under launchd on this machine, so load drifts between an A run and a later B run at exactly that scale. Proposed by the r1-fixes session (sofar-4c) 2026-09-16, adopted here. Large single-order effects (the −33 to −39% write-path gains) stand but are re-confirmed interleaved once.
